newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banacci to merge units with Banamex.
newsitem.headline: Banacci to merge units with Banamex.

text.p: Banacci said on Monday its shareholders approved the merger of its leasing, factoring and foreign exchange units with Banamex, its largest subsidiary, adding that Banamex's stockholders equity will increase by about 1.095 billion pesos as a result.

It said that with the merger Banamex had now completed more than 90 percent of its 8.54 capitalization program that Banacci committed to in December 1995. That program gave the bank the right to sell about 15 billion pesos of net loans to the Bank Insurance Fund, Fobaproa.

The merger will incorporate leasing arm Arrendadora Banamex, factoring firm Banamex Factoraje and Casa de Cambio Euromex, the foreign exchange house, with Banamex, Mexico's largest bank. Banacci said the merger will be based on the financial statements as of August 31 and will come into effect as of September 30.
It leaves Banacci with three direct subsidiaries: Banamex, which handles commercial banking; Acciones y Valores de Mexico (Accival), investment banking; and Seguros Banamex-Aegon, insurance.
Through Banamex, Banacci will continue providing the financial services that were previously provided by the merged units, the financial group said.
